notes.text: Ministered — That is, performed his ministration carefully and faithfully. Before the Lord - In God's tabernacle. Ephod - A garment used in God's service, and allowed not only to the inferior priests and Levites but also to eminent persons of the people, and therefore to Samuel, who, though no Levite, was a Nazarite, from his birth.

glossa.text: *A tunic.* The tunic which Anna, that is grace, made and delivered to the boy; it is the beginning doctrine by which the faithful receive the first rudiments, whence: *I gave you milk to drink, not meat ((I Cor. III))*. But the linen ephod signifies chastity and continence together with good works. For he who desires to minister to the Lord must needs live chastely and continently, and exercise himself in good works.

notes.text: Heavens of heavens — Ye highest heavens, the place of God's throne. Waters - Ye clouds which are above a part of the heavens.
Established — He hath made them constant and incorruptible, not changeable, as the things of the lower world. A decree - Concerning their continuance.
Dragons — Either serpents, which hide in the deep caverns of the earth; or whales, and other sea-monsters, which dwell in the depths of the sea.

Fire — Lightnings and other fireworks of the air. Vapor - Or, fumes: hot exhalations. Fulfilling his word - Executing his commands, either for the comfort or punishment of the inhabitants of the earth.
Above — Above all the glories which are in earth and in heaven.

The horn — In scripture commonly denotes strength, victory, glory, and felicity. An exhortation to praise God for his love to his people, ver. 1-5. And for enabling them to overcome their enemies, ver. 6- 9.

glossa.text: *Praise ye the Lord from the heavens.* ((CASS.)) By the mention of a few he exhorts the whole creation to praise God. There are certain things which have a spirit of praising God in that affection wherewith God pleases them: certain have no understanding, but because they themselves are good in their own order, and are referred to the beauty of the whole, they praise not of themselves, but by them God is praised through those that consider them: and so after a sort they praise, because from them the praise of God is born in us, whereto the prophet here admonishes us.

*For he spoke, and they were made.* ((CASS.)) This against those who say that the world is coeternal with God; there follows: *He commanded.* By his word, and they were created. First he said, *made,* afterward *created.* For make we also can, but not create. He therefore alone creates, which is proper to the Godhead. Praise from his works

*He hath established.* From his power he is almighty, whose works are not changed.

*Unto the age, and unto the age of the age.* ((CAS.)) And though the heaven be new, yet they are said to be well established by God, which are made new through Christ and remain bettered. And here is praise from his power.

*Praise ye the Lady *Dominam*; read *Dominum*, "the Lord".* The second part, where, the heavenly things being enumerated, he descends to earthly things. Turning therefore to them, as exhorting us that by the consideration of them we may praise God, which things considered lay open the praise of God, he says: O ye that are of the earth. *All ye deeps.* *ubyssi* ((AUG.)) The depth of the waters, etc., *as far as* these therefore, that is, he exhorts us to praise by the consideration of them.

*Which do his word.* This therefore because it seemed to certain men that God ruled the higher things, but despised these lower ones, and that they were ruled by chance; but these also God does, and in these least things he is praised, and alleluia is sung.

*Confession.* ((CAS.)) Above he spoke first of heaven, afterward of earth; here of all together. And he takes by heaven all higher things, and by earth all lower things. ((AUG.)) *His confession above heaven and earth.* All things confess him in themselves or in others; the beauty of all things is the voice of them that confess, in those who consider them, that is, let those who consider praise him, both from earthly and from heavenly things, than which there is nothing better.
*He hath exalted the horn of his people.* ((ID.)) Behold what Aggeus and Zacharias prophesied. Now the horn of his people is lowly in tribulations, but when the Lord shall come, it shall be exalted.

notes.text: All who are thus renewed are elected of God, holy, and therefore the more beloved of him. Holiness is the consequence of their election, and God's superior love, of their holiness.
Forbearing one another — If anything is now wrong. And forgiving one another - What is past.
The love of God contains the whole of Christian perfection, and connects all the parts of it together.
And then the peace of God shall rule in your hearts — Shall sway every temper, affection, thought, as the reward (so the Greek word implies) of your preceding love and obedience.

Let the word of Christ — So the apostle calls the whole scripture, and thereby asserts the divinity of his Master. Dwell - Not make a short stay, or an occasional visit, but take up its stated residence. Richly - In the largest measure, and with the greatest efficacy; so as to fill and govern the whole soul.
In the name — In the power and Spirit of the Lord Jesus. Giving thanks unto God - The Holy Ghost. And the Father through him - Christ.

glossa.text: *Charity.* For it is itself the more eminent way, which is above knowledge and all precepts. This is the seamless garment of the Lord, woven from above. Seamless, lest at any time it be unsewn, which reaches to one, because charity gathers all into one.
*Peace.* This is necessary to the unity of the body, which it has itself made. *The peace of God.* There can be called a peace which has not charity; but charity always has peace with itself.
*Teaching and admonishing.* He says this, that there may be teaching for those who know not, and admonition for those who know.

*All whatsoever.* Because above he commanded God to be praised in the heart, now he exhorts that the name of God be praised and exalted both in words and in deeds: so that our words and works may thus lack reproof, that the Lord may be magnified, by whose teaching the disciples are unblameable. *All things.* Not only what you do in word or in deed, but all things, even thoughts, and if there be any others. Or, whatever you do, do the whole, that is, the perfect, by attributing it to God, and this is, doing in the name. *Giving thanks.* Then do we truly give thanks to God through Christ, if we keep the measure of his precepts.

notes.text: The child Jesus — St. Luke describes in order Jesus the fruit of the womb, chap. i, 42; an infant, chap. ii, 12; a little child, ver. 40; a child here, and afterward a man. So our Lord passed through and sanctified every stage of human life. Old age only did not become him.
Supposing him to have been in the company — As the men and women usually travelled in distinct companies.

After three days — The first day was spent in their journey, the second, in their return to Jerusalem: and the third, in searching for him there: they found him in the temple - In an apartment of it: sitting in the midst of the doctors - Not one word is said of his disputing with them, but only of his asking and answering questions, which was a very usual thing in these assemblies, and indeed the very end of them. And if he was, with others, at the feet of these teachers (where learners generally sat) he might be said to be in the midst of them, as they sat on benches of a semicircular form, raised above their hearers and disciples.
Why sought ye me? — He does not blame them for losing, but for thinking it needful to seek him: and intimates, that he could not be lost, nor found any where, but doing the will of a higher parent.
It is observable that Joseph is not mentioned after this time; whence it is probable, he did not live long after.

Jesus increased in wisdom — As to his human nature, and in favour with God - In proportion to that increase. It plainly follows, that though a man were pure, even as Christ was pure, still he would have room to increase in holiness, and in consequence thereof to increase in the favour, as well as in the love of God.

glossa.text: *And his parents went,* etc. ((ID.)) Deservedly Luke is compared, among the four living creatures, to the calf, etc., *as far as* at the end of his Gospel he concludes with the disciples of the Lord praising in the temple.
*And not finding him. ((ID.))* If it is asked how he could be left behind by his parents through forgetfulness, etc., *as far as* returned with the other parent.

*In the midst. ((ID.))* As a fountain, he sits in the midst of the doctors; but as a pattern of humility, he asks and hears before he instructs, lest little ones should blush to be taught by their elders, lest one who is weak should dare to teach.

*How is it that you sought me? ((ID.))* He does not find fault with their seeking him as a son, but he suggests who is his true Father, and compels them to lift the eyes of the mind to what is rather owed to him whose eternal Son he is. For because he is God and man, now he sets forth the lofty things of the Godhead, now the weak things of the humanity. As the Son of God he stays in the temple; as the Son of man he goes back with his parents whither they bid.

*And his mother kept all these words in her heart.* All the things which she knew to have been done concerning the Lord or by the Lord, whether those she understood or those she could not yet understand, she laid up all in her memory, so that, when the time should come for his incarnation to be preached or written, she might be able sufficiently to set forth to those who asked all things just as they had been done. So let us, by frequent meditation on the deeds and words of the Lord, drive off importunate thoughts and labour to instruct others.
*He advanced in wisdom. ((BEDA.))* As it belongs to the flesh to advance in age, etc., *as far as* both alike might be saved.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise him in the heights.
Let us clothe ourselves with love.
The child grew, and the favor of God was upon him.
Let us clothe ourselves with love.
Whatever you do, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Come, let us worship. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: The angels have gone; the shepherds have gone home. The work of an ordinary life begins.
Praise the Lord; let his name be praised.
A boy grows up in Nazareth, year by quiet year, in wisdom and in grace.
Praise the Lord; let his name be praised.
So we put on, like clothing, compassion and kindness and patience.
Praise the Lord; let his name be praised.
And over it all we put on love, which binds everything together.
Praise the Lord; let his name be praised forever!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The shepherds gone home, an ordinary life begins.
Praise the Lord; let his name be praised.
A child grows in wisdom and in grace.
Praise the Lord; let his name be praised.
Clothe yourselves with love, and do all in his name.
Praise the Lord; let his name be praised. Amen.
